{{nihongo|'''Nakagawa Shrine'''|中川神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

=== Annual festival ===
2nd Sunday of April. Nakatsugawa Taiko, Kamiyo-shishi, and others are dedicated.

=== History ===
This is Nakagawa Shrine, a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki-listed shrine}} of {{ill|Ena District, Gifu|ca|Ena|fa|ناحیه انا، گیفو|fr|District d'Ena|ja|恵那郡|qid=Q3030924}}, {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}. It is the {{ill|Ubusunagami|ja|産土神|ko|산토신|zh|產土神|qid=Q1392097}} of Nakatsugawa City.

Founding date is unknown. Since {{ill|Mount Ena|arz|جبل مونت انا|ceb|Ena-san|de|Ena (Berg)|fr|Mont Ena|ja|恵那山|lld|Mont Ena|ml|എന പർവ്വതം|my|အဲနတောင်|pl|Ena (góra)|pnb|ٹلہ اینا|vi|Núi Ena|zh|惠那山|qid=Q1339920}} is regarded as the place where {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu}}'s placenta was placed ({{ill|Ena Shrine (Nakatsugawa)|ja|恵那神社|qid=Q11492453}}), this area is thought to have long been sacred, and there is also a tradition that {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}} was born here.

Formerly it was called Hakusan-sha or Susukinomori. One theory says it began with worship of a goddess of the {{ill|Kiso River|Q779607|qid=Q779607}}, and that this deity was later changed into three goddess deities (Kukuri-hime, Izanami, Konohanasakuya-hime).

The current reading is "Nakagawa," but in older times it was also read "Nakawa" and "Nakatsukawa," and one theory says this gave rise to the place name Nakatsugawa.

Also, the {{ill|Nakatsu River|ja|中津川 (岐阜県)|qid=Q11366440|lt=Nakatsugawa}}, a tributary of the Kiso River, was formerly called Nakagawa.

According to "Mino Kodō Misakagoe-ki" and "Nakagawa Kyūki," it was originally the main Kumano Gongen shrine, and at rebuilding Hakusan Daigongen (Kukuri-hime) was made principal while Kumano (Izanami) and Fuji (Konohanasakuya-hime) were enshrined in the aiden; a {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}} called '''Taishō-ji''' managed the shrine.

The temple site is on the southern foot of Nakagawa Shrine. It is now a residential area, but one hōkyōintō and one gorintō remain. White porcelain-like sherds (yamachawan) were collected from a garden on the ridge connected to Nakagawa Shrine, but it is unclear whether they indicate kiln remains or a dwelling site.

According to "Mino Kodō Misakagoe-ki," in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 2 ({{ill|1574|Q6680|qid=Q6680}}), Hakusan Daigongen was burned by war during {{ill|Takeda Katsuyori|cs|Kacujori Takeda|de|Takeda Katsuyori|eo|Takeda Katsuyori|es|Takeda Katsuyori|eu|Takeda Katsuyori|fa|تاکدا کاتسویوری|fr|Takeda Katsuyori|id|Takeda Katsuyori|it|Takeda Katsuyori|ja|武田勝頼|ko|다케다 가쓰요리|ms|Takeda Katsuyori|nl|Takeda Katsuyori|pl|Katsuyori Takeda|pt|Takeda Katsuyori|ro|Takeda Katsuyori|ru|Такэда Кацуёри|sr|Такеда Кацујори|th|ทาเกดะ คัตสึโยริ|tr|Takeda Katsuyori|uk|Такеда Кацуйорі|zh|武田勝賴|zh_min_nan|Takeda Katuyori|qid=Q662482}}'s invasion of {{ill|Tōnō|Q7862707|qid=Q7862707}}. At that time the middle seat was Hakusan, left Kumano, right Fuji; the ornate shrine and monks' quarters were burned, and only graves of the priest and shrine monks remained.

It was rebuilt in {{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}} 5 ({{ill|1677|Q7631|qid=Q7631}}).

Possibly because of this, in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} only three shrines are seen for {{ill|Nakatsugawa-juku|Q2420820|qid=Q2420820}} on the {{ill|Nakasendō|Q1154479|qid=Q1154479}} (Hachiman shrine, Hakusan Gongen shrine, Shinmei shrine), and the name Nakagawa Shrine disappears. It is thought to have been divided and re-enshrined sometime between the Sengoku-period destruction and the early Edo period.

The current honden is the rebuild of Enpō 5 (1677), but the haiden and related buildings were not rebuilt then. In {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 14 ({{ill|2002|Q1987|qid=Q1987}}), the haiden and naoraiden were rebuilt and the precinct was also improved.

=== Access ===
*About 800 m from {{ill|Nakatsugawa Station|Q5359511|qid=Q5359511}} on the {{ill|Chūō Main Line|Q1078110|qid=Q1078110}}

=== Other ===
*Directly beneath Nakagawa Shrine precinct runs an uphill-line {{ill|Tunnel|Q44377|qid=Q44377}} of the Chūō Main Line.
